title: Apple moves to protect private Mac data from overreaching AI apps
content:
AI apps can reach far beyond the data Mac users intend to share, which has prompted Apple to take action and require clearer consent before granting access.


Apple to tighten Mac Full Disk Access over AI privacy risks
On Friday, Apple announced plans to tighten Full Disk Access controls on the Mac as AI agents gain access to sensitive personal information. The permission lets apps bypass privacy protections and could expose messages, email, files, and browsing history.
Recent incidents involving Meta's Muse and other agents illustrate the risks. Not only can they access sensitive information, OpenAI recently fixed a bug in its Mac app that could have allowed its agent to become corrupted and run malicious commands on behalf of an attacker.

title: Apple Announces 'Full Disk Access' Changes on macOS Due to AI Agents
content:
In a post on its developer news website today, Apple announced that it will be introducing "additional controls" for the "Full Disk Access" setting on macOS due to new risks posed by AI agents. This announcement comes amid the rise of always-on AI agents like Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots, which have prompted privacy concerns.


"Some developers are using Full Disk Access in ways that could put users at risk, exposing everything on their systems—including files, mail, messages, and even browsing history—without users' full knowledge and understanding," said Apple.

"As AI agents become increasingly capable and autonomous, the risks associated with this level of access will grow substantially," it added.

We give developers powerful APIs to build incredible capabilities into their apps for Apple products, backed by a set of controls designed to protect users' private data. Full Disk Access largely sidesteps these controls in order to allow backup apps to function properly on the Mac. Some developers are using Full Disk Access in ways that could put users at risk, exposing everything on their systems—including files, mail, messages, and even browsing history—without users' full knowledge and understanding. For communication apps, this can also compromise the privacy of the people users are communicating with.

Apple did not say when the new "Full Disk Access" controls will be implemented.

title: AT&T and Apple Just Took Steps Toward Fixing iPhone 18 Pro Max Issue
content:
AT&T and Apple are taking action today as they try to resolve iPhone 18 Pro Max cellular issues, according to MacRumors contributor Aaron Perris.


Thousands of iPhone 18 Pro Max users have been unable to connect to the AT&T network for phone calls, text messages, and data. The underlying cause has yet to be disclosed, but AT&T and Apple continue to work toward a resolution.

First, Apple today released an AT&T carrier settings update (version 72.1, up from 72.0.2) for iPhones. Given the timing of this update, it presumably includes some optimizations related to iPhone 18 Pro Max cellular connectivity, but it is unclear if AT&T has fully resolved the issues or if further tweaks will be necessary.

carrier settings update is available on your iPhone, you will be prompted to install it. If you dismiss the notification or do not see it, open the Settings app, tap General → About, and the update should appear there. You can see your iPhone's current carrier settings version in the same About menu, next to your carrier's name.

title: Coming to Apple TV: All the upcoming shows, movies, trailers, and more
content:
Macworld





Apple’s list of currently available content for Apple TV continues to grow, and so does the list of upcoming projects in the works.
Some of these projects have been officially announced and acknowledged by Apple, while others have been reported by the Hollywood press.
We’ve divided this list in two: Coming Soon is a list of shows and films for which Apple has given an official release date or release window, and Further Out compiles content that is still in production or perhaps haven’t even begun yet.
Updated October 2, 2026: We have updated our list with the latest release dates, images, and trailers.
How to get Apple TV
Apple TV 4K (2022, 3. Gen.) 128GB WiFi + Ethernet
							

										
									Read our review
									
							
$129 at Apple							
						
You can subscribe to Apple TV on Apple’s website here, or via the Apple TV app on your device. It costs $12.99/£9.99 a month, which you can cancel at any time (Read: How to cancel and Apple subscription). You can also opt for a one-year subscription for $99/£89, which gives you two months free each year.
Apple also offers various trials. Take a look at our article explaining all the ways you can watch Apple TV for free, and the best Apple TV deals you can get. Students can get Apple TV for free with an already subsidized Apple Music subscription.
You don’t need an Apple TV set top box to watch Apple TV, nor do you have to pay for a subscription, see: How to watch Apple TV for free.
Coming Soon to Apple TV
The following shows, series, and movies have been officially announced by Apple and will typically will begin streaming in the next few weeks or months.
Small Prophets
What it’s about: Michael Sleep is still struggling after his girlfriend, Clea, vanished seven years earlier. Sleep works in a DIY store, visits his dad Brian and hopes for Clea’s return. This series first debuted on the BBC.

				
					

				
			
Apple




Important names: Stars Mackenzie Crook, Pearce Quigley, Lauren Patel, and Sir Michael Palin.
When you can watch: Small Prophets premieres on October 7, 2026.
Matchbox the Movie
What it’s about: Inspired by the iconic Mattel toys (really!), this is an action film about a group of friends since childhood who have their lives upended when undercover CIA agent Sean, their long-absent former leader, returns to their small town and unwittingly gets them embroiled in a frantic international pursuit to save the world.






Important names: Stars John Cena, Jessica Biel, Sam Richardson, and Arturo Castro. Written by David Coggeshall. Directed by Sam Hargrave.
When you can watch: Matchbox the Movie will premiere on October 9, 2026.
Tenzing
What it’s about: Chronicles the little-known story of Tenzing Norgay, a gifted Himalayan climber who, alongside New Zealand mountaineer Edmund Hillary, became the first to summit Mount Everest.

				
					

				
			
Apple




Important names: Stars Genden Phuntsok, Tom Hiddleston, and Willem Dafoe.
When you can watch: Tenzing is in select theaters on October 9 and on Apple TV October 16.
Where’s Wanda (season 2)
What it’s about: A dark comedy that tells the story of Dedo and Carlotta Klatt, who are desperate to locate their missing 17-year-old daughter Wanda, who disappeared months ago without a trace.

				
					

				
			
Apple




Important names: Stars Heike Makatsch, Axel Stein, Lea Drinda, and Leo Simon. Written and created by Oliver Lansley.
When you can watch: The second season of Where’s Wanda premieres on October 21, 2026.
Nocturne
What it’s about: The series tells the story of an ex-soldier turned homicide detective Jonah Lynn who moves to a small town in western Pennsylvania for a quiet life. But, as the town and his family come under attack from the diabolically cunning serial killer Jurek Walter, Jonah must protect all that he holds dear.

				
					

				
			
Apple




Important names: Stars Liev Schreiber, Zazie Beetz, Stephen Graham, and Bill Camp. Directed by Tim Van Patten and Allen Coulter.
When you can watch: Nocturne premieres on October 30, 2026.
Stick (season 2)
What it’s about: A sports comedy about a washed-up ex-pro golfer who coaches a young 17-year old phenom.

				
					

				
			
Apple




Important names: Starring Owen Wilson, Peter Dager, Marc Maron, Mariana Treviño. Joining in season 2 is Rhea Seehorn.
When you can watch: Season 2 of Stick premieres on November 4, 2026.
Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook
What it’s about: Hollywood actor and comedian Nora Lum (aka Awkwafina) is the descendant of restaurant royalty … but she can’t cook. Join the star on an inspiring culinary road trip as she learns the craft and attempts to revive her family’s beloved Chinese eatery.






Important names: Stars Nora Lum, also known as Awkwafina.
When you can watch: Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook premieres on November 6, 2026.
12 12 12
What it’s about: Each episode of 12 12 12 unfolds across three timelines of a heist: the 12 months of planning, the 12 hours of the heist and the 12 days following it.

				
					

				
			
Apple




Important names: Stars Anthony Mackie, Jamie Dornan, Jack Kesy, and Agathe Rousselle.
When you can watch: 12 12 12 premieres on November 13, 2026.
Being Heumann
What it’s about: In 1977, a young disabled woman Judy Heumann and a scrappy coalition of outsiders decide they’ve had enough. What begins as one impulsive act becomes the longest occupation of a federal building in American history, as hundreds spontaneously seize government offices and refuse to leave until the bureaucrat in their way takes action.

				
					

				
			
Apple




Important names: Stars Ruth Madeley, Madeline Delp, and Mark Ruffalo. Written and directed by Siân Heder.
When you can watch: Being Heumann will be in select theaters on November 6 and on Apple TV November 13, 2026,
Way of the Warrior Kid
What it’s about: Middle school has been a nightmare for Marc, a good kid who’s bullied by his classmates and feels like he’s behind in everything, from academics to P.E. to just making friends. That changes when his injured Uncle Jake, a decorated Navy SEAL, comes to spend the summer and recuperate with Marc and his mom, Sarah.

				
					

				
			
Apple




Important names: Stars Chris Pratt, Jude Hill, Linda Cardellini, Levi McConaughey.
When you can watch: Way of the Warrior Kid premieres on November 20, 2026. 
Bad Monkey (season 2)
What it’s about: Eager to regain his detective’s badge, Yancy finds himself embroiled in a turf war between rival criminal organizations as he navigates a variety of Florida oddballs, including an erudite mob boss, his unhinged son and a hard-edged young woman who needs Yancy’s protection.

				
					

				
			
Apple




Important names: Stars Vince Vaughn, Rob Delaney, Meredith Hagner. Produced by Bill Lawrence.
When you can watch: The second season of Bad Monkey premieres on December 2, 2026.
Neuromancer
What it’s about: A new 10-episode drama based on the award-winning novel of the same name by William Gibson. The series will follow a damaged, top-rung super-hacker named Case who is thrust into a web of digital espionage and high-stakes crime with his partner Molly, a razor-girl assassin with mirrored eyes, aiming to pull a heist on a corporate dynasty with untold secrets.






Important names: Stars Callum Turner, Briana Middleton, Mark Strong, and Peter Sarsgaard.
When you can watch: Neuromancer premieres on January 22, 2027.
Further Out
These shows, series, and movies may or may not have been officially announced, and do not yet have definitive release dates. Some may debut in the next few months, others be more than a year away. It’s even possible that some of these projects will never be released.
Lance Armstrong biopic
What it’s about: Deadline reports that Apple has won the bidding war for rights to a movie about the storied cyclist Lance Armstrong.
Important names: Stars Austin Butler, directed by Edward Berger.
When you can watch: The Lance Armstrong biopic does not yet have a title or release date.
Foster the Snowman
What it’s about: Per Deadline, Apple out-bid Netflix and MGM for this holiday high-concept movie about a snowman that comes alive, and will go through every stage of life in just 72 hours. The childless couple who act as his “parents” go through every parenting milestone in just three days.
Important names: No stars are yet attached. The film will be directed by Hikari.
When you can watch: Foster the Snowman is being fast-tracked to be ready in time for the holidays 2026.
Once and Again
What it’s about: Deadline says that Apple won the rights to produce a film from the upcoming romance book Once and Again by Rebecca Serle (set to release on March 10). 
Important names: This project is early in product and has no director or stars attached yet.
When you can watch: The adaptation of Once and Again is very early in production and has no release date.
Cosmere
What it’s about: Apple has landed the rights to the Cosmere fantasy universe books from Brandon Sanderson. It’s unclear what projects are coming in this fantasy setting.
Important names: Brandon Sanderson’s series The Stormlight Archive is a large and ongoing series of high fantasy novels. Sanderson is also known for finishing Robert Jordan’s Wheel of Time novels.
When you can watch: The Cosmere deal is fresh and specific projects haven’t yet begun as of January 2026, so it will be a long while before we can watch anything.
Important names: Created for TV by Graham Roland and JD Dillard. Stars Callum Turner, Briana Middleton, Joseph Lee, and Mark Strong.
When you can watch: Neuromancer is in production now but does not yet have a release date.
The Dispatcher
What it’s about: A 6-episode thriller about a police detective whose life fell apart 10 years ago when his young daughter Maggie disappeared without a trace. Now working as a police dispatcher, he receives a distress call from a young girl he is certain is Maggie, he will stop at nothing to find her and reunite his broken family, whatever the cost. Adapted from Ryan David Jahn’s book.
Important names: Starring Patrick Brammall, adapted by writer Kris Mrksa.
When you can watch: The Dispatcher does not yet have a release date.
Speed Racer
What it’s about: A live-action series based on the beloved Japanese animated show from the ’60s. 
Important names: Will be produced by J.J. Abrams’ Bad Robot production company, with Hiram Martinez and Ron Fitzgerald as writers and showrunners.
When you can watch: Speed Racer has no release date yet.
The White Darkness
What it’s about: A limited series based on David Grann’s nonfiction book about Henry Worsley, who crossed Antarctica on foot.
Important names: Tom Hiddleston stars, Soo Hugh directs.
When you can watch: The White Darkness has no release date yet.
Untitled Negro League Baseball series
What it’s about: Follows the life and career of legendary pitcher Leroy “Satchel” Paige. 
Important names: The series is produced by Erving “Magic” Johnson, among others. It is in conjunction with the Negro Leagues Baseball Museum and MLB.
When you can watch: This series has no release date yet.
Untitled Chuck Barris drama
What it’s about: Gong Show host Chuck Barris famously claimed to be a secret CIA assassin in his autobiography Confessions of a Dangerous Mind, which was made into a feature film in 2002. A Deadline report says Apple is developing an hour-long drama series about Barris as both Gong Show host and CIA assassin.
Important names: Justin Timberlake is attached to star as Chuck Barris.
When you can watch: This series has no release date yet.  
Dolly
What it’s about: Deadline describes it as a “sci-fi courtroom drama in which a robotic ‘companion doll’ kills its owner and then shocks the world by claiming that she is not guilty and asking for a lawyer.”
Important names: Florence Pugh and Vanessa Taylor are attached to star and Drew Pearce will write the script.
When you can watch: No release date yet.
Bride
What it’s about: Deadline reports that this is a genre-bending film about an engineered “ideal wife” who rejects her creator, escapes captivity, and discovers her true self.
Important names: The film will star Scarlett Johansson and will be directed by Sebastián Lelio.
When you can watch: No release date yet.
Earthsound
What it’s about: A natural history documentary series that uses new audio technology and cinematic 360-degree audio to reveal untold nature stories from every continent.
Important names: It will be executive produced by Alex Williamson, and the series producer is Sam Hodgson.
When you can watch: No release date yet.
Untitled Idris Elba spy thriller
What it’s about: According to Variety, this is to be a “spy movie with romance set in Africa” but little else is known about the nascent project. The report says it’s early in production. 
Important names: The film will star Idris Elba and is produced by Simon Kinberg and Audrey Chon.
When you can watch: No release date yet.
Hedy Lamarr series
What it’s about: According to The Hollywood Reporter, it’s an eight-episode series about the 1930s and 40s actress and inventor Hedy Lamarr (whose frequency-hopping radio technology is still the basis for many modern wireless communications).
Important names: Gal Gadot is set to star as Lamarr, with a script written by Sarah Treem.
When you can watch: No release date yet.
Where the Wild Things Are
What it’s about: Apple has struck an overall deal with The Maurice Sendak Foundation to produce shows or series based on the author’s works for children. The most famous of these, by far, is Where the Wild Things Are.
Important names: Apple is working with longtime Sendak collaborator Arthur Yorinks and his production studio Night Kitchen Studios.
When you can watch: No release date yet.
Custom of the Country
What it’s about: A limited-series adaptation of the Edith Wharton novel The Custom of the Country. The novel, published in the early 20th century, is about a midwestern girl who climbs the ladder of New York high society.
Important names: The big one is Sofia Coppola, who is developing the series for Apple. No word yet on whether she will direct it.
When you can watch: No release date yet.
El Gato Negro
What it’s about: Based on Richard Dominguez’s comic book about an aging luchador who teams up with his grandson to use the El Gato Negro persona to fight crime in South Texas.
Important names: Robert Rodriguez will direct and produce, while Diego Boneta will star and also produce.
When you can watch: No release date yet.
Brie Larson CIA biography series
What it’s about: A report in Variety says that Apple has made a direct-to-series order for a new drama based on the real-life experiences of CIA undercover operative Amaryllis Fox. Fox has a hot novel named Life Undercover: Coming of Age in the CIA that released in October 2019. 
Important names: Brie Larson will star and executive produce the series.
When you can watch: No release date yet.
You Think It, I’ll Say It
What it’s about:  According to Variety, Apple has ordered a 10-episode, half-hour run of a new comedy variety show. The show is inspired by Curtis Sittenfeld’s collection of short stories You Think It, I’ll Say It.
Important names: SNL alum Kristen Wiig was set to star, but pulled out citing scheduling conflicts with Wonder Woman 1984. The show is created and produced by Colleen McGuinness (30 Rock, About a Boy).
When you can watch: This project does not yet have a title or release date.

Apple released AirPods Pro 3 in September 2025. They brought a slightly new design with foam-infused tips for a better fit. They also brought several new features, including an in-ear heart rate sensor, better battery life, enhanced noise cancellation, and improved sound.
They are especially worth considering if you want the strongest earbud noise cancellation, a secure in-ear fit or Apple’s hearing-health features; battery life is rated at up to eight hours with ANC.

The $129 version includes a USB-C charging case, while the $149 Wireless Charging Case version adds wireless charging, longer battery life, a Find My speaker and volume adjustment by swiping the stems.
Compare the prices of both packages before buying. A discount on the basic version may look attractive, but the wireless-charging package could offer better value if the price difference is small.

Amazon Prime Day AirPods deals to avoid
Compare older AirPods with the discounted price of their replacements. A large reduction from an old launch price can still represent poor value. Check the generation, charging case, condition and seller before ordering.
Be wary of promotions that advertise “free” AirPods. These offers often require long-term financial commitments or involve complicated rebate processes. For example, a recent Apple Card promotion offered AirPods Pro 3 for signing up, but only through a reimbursement scheme outlined in the fine print.
You should also be cautious with marketplace and third-party sellers offering supposedly new AirPods at prices dramatically below those from established retailers. Counterfeit models are common and are often advertised at discounts far below Apple’s normal pricing. If a deal seems too good to be true, it’s worth checking whether the product is genuine. Prime Day is widely considered one of the best times of the year to buy Apple products, alongside Black Friday in November. However, there are a few things to consider before making a purchase:
Prime Membership Requirement: Many of the best deals are exclusive to Amazon Prime members. If you’re not already subscribed, you can take advantage of Amazon’s 30-day free trial or sign up for a month and cancel afterward if you don’t plan to keep the membership. Prime membership costs $139 / £95 / AUD$59 annually, or $14.99 / £8.99 / AU$6.99 on a monthly basis. As well as getting free two-day shipping, Prime customers also get access to Prime Video and Music.
Alternative Sales: If you miss Prime Day, the Black Friday sales in November will be the next opportunity to get discounts.
Compare Prices: Amazon isn’t always the cheapest option. Retailers such as Walmart and Best Buy frequently run competing “anti-Prime Day” promotions, so it’s worth comparing prices before buying.
Prime Day is available in multiple countries, including Australia, Austria, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, China, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Luxembourg, Mexico, the Netherlands, Portugal, Singapore, Spain, the U.K., and the U.S.

Why you can trust Macworld’s recommendations
The AirPods picked here are all chosen by our editors, who have decades of experience with Apple devices. We’ve reviewed everything we recommend, and we won’t tell you to buy something that’s not actually worth your money.

title: AT&T on iPhone 18 Pro Max Issues: 'We Are Working With Apple'
content:
In a statement shared with MacRumors today, AT&T said it is "working with Apple" to resolve iPhone 18 Pro Max cellular issues.


"Apple has released a software update to address an issue that may affect calls, data, texts, and 911 calls on a small number of Apple iPhone 18 Pro Max phones," an AT&T spokesperson said. "AT&T customers with an iPhone 18 Pro Max should update their phones now to the latest available software. Our top priority is ensuring customers can stay connected when they need it most, and we are working with Apple to make it right."

reported last week, affected iPhone 18 Pro Max users are unable to connect to the AT&T network for phone calls, text messages, or data either persistently or intermittently, and their devices typically enter SOS mode as a result. The underlying cause has not been confirmed, and Apple has yet to publicly comment on the matter.

Apple Support Community, Reddit, MacRumors Forums, and other online platforms.

equipped with a Qualcomm cellular modem. The smaller iPhone 18 Pro and the iPhone Duo are equipped with Apple's C2 modem worldwide, as is the iPhone 18 Pro Max in all other countries. However, it is unclear if this is a contributing factor.

AT&T said iPhone 18 Pro Max users who have experienced or continue to experience issues can return to an Apple or AT&T store for additional support.

advising them to update to iOS 27.0.1 immediately, even though that update does not appear to resolve the issues, according to comments shared by affected users.

shared on Reddit today, AT&T clarified that its guidance about updating to iOS 27.0.1 is meant to help mitigate future impacts, but it is unclear if or how the update actually helps. Apple's release notes for iOS 27.0.1 only mentioned fixes for other bugs, including a Face ID issue affecting iPhone 18 Pro models.

The alleged email added that customers can visit an Apple or AT&T store for a replacement device, but some customers said their request for a replacement under warranty was declined. title: Upgrading From an Older Apple Watch? Here's How the New Features Stack Up
content:
The Apple Watch has received some incremental updates in recent years, with significant upgrades becoming fewer and farther between as the device has progressed. Since the Apple Watch's generation-over-generation enhancements are relatively small, it is all the more important to consider when an upgrade is justified and whether an older model could suffice for your needs.


The Apple Watch Series 12 brings a more substantial set of changes than the Series 11, which was one of the smallest refreshes in the device's history. While Apple has discontinued previous Series models, older watches may still be available at lower prices from third-party retailers or secondhand.

Read on to see the breakdown below for each new feature, change, and improvement that was added with each Apple Watch model compared to its direct predecessor. Viewing each generation's changes in this way helps weigh up the accumulative upgrades one receives by skipping multiple generations when buying a new device, as well as get a sense of which generations offered the biggest overall upgrades.

Apple Watch Series 12 (2026)

18K Gold and Rose Gold Apple Watch Edition discontinued, Ceramic model introduced in White

The Series 12 has a stronger case than the Series 11 as an upgrade in general, but most Series 11 owners still have little reason to get a new device. Its new heart sensors, more frequent HRV measurements, Readiness app, and longer workout battery life matter most if you rely on your Apple Watch for training and recovery insights. Sound Recognition may also appeal to deaf or hard of hearing users, while the ceramic case offers a finish unavailable with the Series 11. 

Upgrading from a Series 10 brings these changes alongside the Series 11's 5G connectivity on cellular models and longer rated everyday battery life. From a Series 9, you would also gain the thinner Series 10 design, larger display, depth gauge, and water temperature sensor.

The cumulative upgrades become more compelling for Series 8 users and older, particularly if battery wear is affecting daily use. Series 7 owners gain Crash Detection and temperature sensing as well as the newer design and Series 12 health features. The biggest differences will be felt by those with a Series 6 or older, though the condition of your current watch and the cost of replacing it still matter.

watchOS 27 supports Series 9 and later, leaving the Series 8 and older without the latest major software release. That does not mean they will immediately stop working or receiving all security updates, but they are now considered old devices. If you are shopping for a replacement, a discounted or secondhand Series 11 may offer better value if you do not need the Series 12's health features, providing you can find it at a sufficiently low price. watchOS 26 is not supported by the Series 5 or older, so anyone with one of these devices should definitely consider upgrading soon.

Which Apple Watch should you buy this Prime Day

				
					

				
			
David Price / Foundry




Choosing the right Apple Watch depends on your specific needs, whether you are looking for a rugged outdoor companion, a feature-rich flagship, or a budget-friendly entry point into the ecosystem. Our top recommendation for this Prime Day is the Apple Watch Series 12.
Apple Watch Series 12: Best for most users
Buy the Series 12 if you want Apple’s latest health features without the size and expense of the Ultra. It combines the new Health Sensing System with a 24-hour battery rating and starts at $399/£369.
Apple Watch Ultra 4: Best for endurance and outdoor use
Choose the Ultra 4 if you need 50-hour battery life, satellite connectivity, precision GPS, diving support or extended workout tracking.
Apple Watch SE 3: Best budget option
The SE 3 is the cheapest current Apple Watch and provides most of the core smartwatch, fitness and safety experience. Its main omissions are Apple’s more advanced health sensors.
Series 11 and Ultra 3: Best clearance opportunities
Don’t automatically dismiss last year’s watches. If retailers heavily discount remaining stock, Series 11 and Ultra 3 could offer better value than the new models.
For more advice read our Best Apple Watch guide.  






Is an older Apple Watch a good Prime Day deal?

				
					

				
			
David Price / Foundry




Don’t assume an older Apple Watch is a bad buy. The Series 11 and Ultra 3 are only one generation old and can make excellent buys if they’re substantially cheaper than the Series 12 or Ultra 4.
Be much more cautious with the Series 8, SE 2 and original Ultra, however. Those models cannot run watchOS 27. The Series 9 is the oldest standard Apple Watch compatible with watchOS 27, while the Ultra 2 is the oldest supported Ultra.
Also compare the sale price with the newest equivalent. A $50 Series 11 saving, for example, may not be enough to justify giving up the Series 12’s new health features, whereas a substantially larger saving could change the calculation.
Should you buy GPS or Cellular?
Don’t automatically pay extra for cellular. The Series 12 costs $100/£100 more with cellular, while the SE 3 premium is $50/£70. Cellular is included with every Ultra 4. For many users, GPS is sufficient because the Watch can still track workouts, use Apple Pay and play downloaded music without an iPhone. Cellular becomes most useful if you regularly leave your iPhone behind but still want calls, messages and online services. Read: Do I need a cellular Apple Watch?






Should you buy an Apple Watch during Amazon Prime Day?
Amazon’s October Prime Day sale is unusually well timed for Apple Watch buyers because Apple’s 2026 models have only just arrived. If the Series 12 or Ultra 4 is discounted, you can buy the newest generation without paying Apple’s full launch price.
It’s also an excellent time to look at previous-generation stock. Series 11 and Ultra 3 are still relatively recent watches, and retailers may discount them aggressively now that their replacements are available.
The other option is to wait until Black Friday in November. If an October deal is modest and you aren’t in a hurry, Black Friday may bring another opportunity – but there’s no guarantee that a particular configuration or older model will remain in stock. Read: When is the best time to buy an Apple Watch?
Before you buy, keep the following in mind:
Prime Membership Requirement: Many of the best deals are exclusive to Amazon Prime members. If you’re not a Prime subscriber, you can take advantage of Amazon’s 30-day free trial or sign up for a month and cancel afterward. Prime membership costs $139 / £95 / AUD$59 annually, or $14.99 / £8.99 / AU$6.99 on a monthly basis. As well as getting free two-day shipping, Prime customers also get access to Prime Video and Music.
Compare Prices: Amazon isn’t always the cheapest retailer. Stores such as Walmart and Best Buy often run competing promotions during Prime Day, so it’s worth checking prices elsewhere before making a purchase.
Alternative Sales: Missed Prime Day? Similar discounts often return during the Black Friday sales in November.
Student Savings: Students may find better value through Apple’s Education Store.  
Prime Day deals are available in multiple countries, including Australia, Austria, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, China, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Luxembourg, Mexico, the Netherlands, Portugal, Singapore, Spain, the U.K., and the U.S.






Why you can trust Macworld’s recommendations
We have decades of experience with Apple devices and have tested and reviewed every Apple Watch since the original model. Everything we recommend has been thoroughly tested and weighed against its contemporaries and previous models.
We don’t recommend products we wouldn’t buy, and we don’t point out a deal unless it’s actually a deal—a product that can always be found at the “sale” price really isn’t on sale. Macworld checks Prime Day deals, comparing against MSRP, price history, model relevance and deal quality before we give our recommendation.

title: AT&T floats a fix for iPhone cellular issues but it doesn’t appear to work
content:
Macworld





Following numerous complaints from iPhone 18 Pro Max owners, it’s now been officially acknowledged that some units have a problem placing calls, sending texts, and accessing data. Not by Apple itself, but by the carrier AT&T, which has sent out a message to customers warning about the issue and strongly advising them to update iOS “immediately”.
As seen by MacRumors, the carrier sent out the following text on Thursday:
“Hi, it’s AT&T. Action needed: An important Apple software update for your iPhone 18 Pro Max is available. Some phones may be unable to complete calls/text/data, including to 911. Update to iOS 27.0.1 immediately — Settings > General > Software Update. Please contact AT&T or Apple if you have questions.”
While this formal admission will be some comfort to affected parties–since the first step on the road to a fix is admitting that one is needed–the proposed solution may not be viewed kindly. Apple’s release notes for the iOS 27.0.1 software update do not mention fixing this issue, which is hardly a surprise given that the company (unlike AT&T) hasn’t yet acknowledged it. And many users who’ve encountered the bug explicitly report that updating to 27.0.1 doesn’t fix it.
The problem was first reported in mid-September. “New [iPhone 18 Pro Max] can’t make or receive phone calls or FaceTime,” complained the author of one Apple Support discussion thread. “Text messages are extremely slow to come through… It does all of this even when the phone is showing four bars of 5G… then the phone randomly drops service and goes into SOS.”
A Redditor, meanwhile, wrote: “I got my iPhone 18 on Friday. I have coverage through AT&T. I have been noticing that I have been getting SOS on my phone. Wi-Fi works for the internet but I can’t make calls. Even if it doesn’t say SOS, trying to make a phone call is impossible now.”
There are thousands of replies to these and similar discussions, many of whom confirm they’ve had the same experience. And they are pessimistic about AT&T’s solution. One commenter on the Apple Support thread replies, “I just received a text from them that the latest [iOS 27.0.1] update would fix the problem – I had already updated to this so I know it isn’t the resolution. This just reaffirms that they have no idea what the problem is or how to fix it.”
And while a separate Reddit thread entitled “iPhone 18 Pro Max Cellular Issues: Did iOS 27.0.1 resolve them?” includes a couple of replies who cautiously think it may have helped, but overwhelming people are unconvinced the issue is fixed:
“No, it did not fix that issue. Can confirm personally.”
“No… The bugfix update did nothing.”
“I feel like the 27.0.1 update made it worse.”
“I did the update but still have the problem.”
“I’m still having the issue even after the update, so it’s definitely AT&T.”
“I updated and it didn’t fix it and had to get the phone replaced for SECOND time.”
It would appear that we’re not even close to a resolution, since it isn’t even clear if this is a hardware or software problem, or whether it’s possible to fix it through an iOS update. We’ll keep you updated as we hear more.
Update, October 2: AT&T sent us the following statement:
“Apple has released a software update to address an issue that may affect calls, data, texts and 911 calls on a small number of Apple iPhone 18 Pro Max phones. AT&T customers with an iPhone 18 Pro Max should update their phones now to the latest available software. Our top priority is ensuring customers can stay connected when they need it most, and we are working with Apple to make it right.”

Which MacBook should you buy?

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Apple’s current MacBook range falls into three clear categories:
MacBook Air M5: Best MacBook for most people
The M5 MacBook Air is our default recommendation for most buyers. It combines strong performance, long battery life and portability without the higher price of a MacBook Pro. With no replacement expected until 2027, a good Prime Day discount would be easy to recommend.
MacBook Neo: Best budget MacBook
The MacBook Neo is the cheapest MacBook and is best suited to students and anyone who mainly needs a laptop for web browsing, documents, streaming and video calls. If a discounted MacBook Air is only moderately more expensive, however, the Air is the better long-term buy.
MacBook Pro M5: Best for demanding work
The MacBook Pro is the better choice for video editing, software development, 3D work and other demanding tasks that benefit from sustained performance. Prime Day discounts could be worthwhile, although a redesigned MacBook Pro is rumored before the end of 2026.
MacBook Pro M5 Pro/Max: Best for professional workloads
Choose an M5 Pro or M5 Max model if you need significantly more CPU and GPU performance, additional memory or greater connectivity. If you already own an M4 Pro or M4 Max model, there is little reason to upgrade.
For most Prime Day shoppers, we recommend starting with the 13-inch M5 MacBook Air. The MacBook Neo becomes especially compelling when heavily discounted, while MacBook Pro buyers should consider whether they need the additional performance and professional features enough to justify the considerably higher price.

Which Mac desktop should you buy?

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Mac mini M6: Best desktop for most people
The new M6 Mac mini is our default desktop recommendation. It starts at $899/£899 and is ideal for home offices, general productivity, coding, photo editing and less demanding creative work. Because it launched only in September, a significant Prime Day discount would be particularly attractive.
Mac mini M5 Pro: Best compact professional desktop
Choose the M5 Pro model if you need more CPU and GPU performance, Thunderbolt 5, greater memory bandwidth or more than 32GB of unified memory.
Mac Studio M5 Max: Best professional workstation
The M5 Max Mac Studio offers considerably greater GPU performance, more memory and more connectivity than the Mac mini and is our preferred Studio configuration for most professional users.
iMac: Best all-in-one
The M4 iMac remains the obvious choice if you want an integrated 4.5K display and minimal desk clutter, but its older M4 chip and $1,499/£1,499 starting price mean we’d only recommend it with a substantial discount.
For more advice read:
Should I buy a Mac mini?
Should I buy a Mac Studio?






Prime Day Mac & MacBook deals to avoid
The cheapest Mac isn’t always the best value. Rather than using Prime Day simply to spend less, use it as an opportunity to get better specifications for the same budget.
When buying a Mac in 2026, try to get as much RAM and storage as you can afford. Most current Macs now start with 16GB of unified memory, although some still have only 256GB of storage. The main exception for memory is the entry-level MacBook Neo, which has 8GB of RAM and a 256GB SSD.
Because Apple silicon Macs can’t have their unified memory or internal storage upgraded later, it’s worth buying enough for your future needs. Memory is particularly important for demanding creative work, development and AI workloads.
For most buyers, prioritizing memory will provide greater long-term benefits than paying extra for a faster processor. Professional users may want 36GB or more, while 64GB or more can be worthwhile for demanding video production, software development and AI workloads.
Don’t buy a MacBook Neo simply because it’s the cheapest Mac: If an M5 Air is only around $200/£200 more, the Air gives you 16GB RAM, better display support and considerably more headroom.
Don’t pay close to full price for an M4 Mac mini: It has now been replaced. Clearance is only attractive if the discount properly reflects that.
Don’t confuse M6 Mac mini with M5 Pro Mac mini: M6 is the mainstream chip; M5 Pro remains much faster for many professional workloads despite the apparently older number. Macworld
Don’t buy a MacBook Pro purely because the discount looks enormous: Apple increased MSRP dramatically in June, so a “$400 off” deal may simply bring it closer to what the machine cost before the increase. Compare the actual selling price with the historic lows in your table.






Should you buy a MacBook or Mac during Prime Day?
October Prime Day is a good opportunity to buy a Mac, but whether you should take a deal depends on the model.
The M5 MacBook Air is particularly easy to recommend because it is not expected to be replaced until 2027. The new M6 and M5 Pro Mac mini are also safe purchases from a product-cycle perspective, although their recent launch means discounts may initially be smaller.
MacBook Pro buyers have a more difficult decision. The current M5 models are powerful machines and a large discount may outweigh the benefit of waiting, but a redesigned MacBook Pro is rumored before the end of 2026.
MacBook Neo buyers should watch the price closely. The previous Prime Day low was $589.99/£549, so a deal near or below those figures would be especially attractive.
We would avoid the iMac because of it’s typically high price and age. 
Finally, remember that Amazon isn’t the only retailer likely to cut prices during Prime Day. Best Buy, Walmart and B&H in the U.S., and retailers including Currys, John Lewis and others in the U.K., may run competing promotions, so compare prices before buying.
Before you buy, keep the following in mind:
Prime membership is required: Many of the best deals are exclusive to Amazon Prime members. If you’re not already subscribed, you might be able to take advantage of Amazon’s 30-day free trial or you could sign up for a month and cancel afterward. As well as getting free two-day shipping, Prime customers also get access to Prime Video and Music. Prime memberships cost $139 / £95 annually, or $14.99 / £8.99 / AU$6.99 every month. 
Other sales: If you miss Prime Day, you’ll have another chance to save during the Black Friday sales in November.
Student Discounts: Students can get discounts at Apple’s Education Store. See: Apple’s U.S. Education Store or Apple’s U.K. Education Store.
Prime Day is available in multiple countries, including Australia, Austria, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, China, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Luxembourg, Mexico, the Netherlands, Portugal, Singapore, Spain, the U.K., and the U.S.







Why you can trust Macworld’s recommendations
The MacBooks and Mac desktops picked here are all chosen by our editors, who have decades of experience with Apple devices. We’ve reviewed everything we recommend, and we only highlight deals that are genuinely good value.
The products selected in this article are at the best current price, usually at or near all-time low prices, and we’ve selected what we think is the best configuration for each product type. We know Apple is expensive, so we’ve chosen products at prices we would be willing to pay, so you can trust that our recommendations will steer you in the right direction.

title: Apple is selling a $19 fix for iPhone Duo creasing
content:
Macworld





Apple has done as much as it can to minimize the visibility of the crease on the iPhone Duo, including multiple shifting display layers and a matte nano-texture surface that reduces glare and makes the crease less visible. But physics is what it is, and you just can’t fold and unfold a display thousands of times without any visible crease forming. The good news is, Apple has another solution to help mitigate that: a replaceable outer layer.
Speaking to @angietutorials on TikTok, Apple’s VP of hardware engineering, Kate Bergeron said, “the matte layer does a really nice job of, I’ll say minimizing the crease, but there’s a cover layer on top and we’ve done a significant amount of engineering work to help that wear in as long a manner as we can, to make sure you get the most out of that layer’s performance. It’s actually replaceable, which is a really nice thing for the customer, that you can peel off that layer and get a new one.”
The AppleCare service and repair site has already been updated with the costs of some repairs for the iPhone Duo with AppleCare+, and it looks like it’s only $19 to get the cover layer replaced. Just note, the top cover layer is not user replaceable like a screen protector would be, though, so don’t go peeling off your iPhone Duo display by yourself.
Apple does not yet list the cost of this service if you don’t have AppleCare+, but it is common for outer glass repairs or replacements to cost $100-150 more without coverage.

title: Best iPhone 18 cases for iPhone 18 Pro & 18 Pro Max
content:
Macworld





You waited months for Apple’s new iPhones to arrive, but it’s worth protecting that big investment from day one. The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are tougher than previous generations, but they can still be scratched, chipped or damaged in a drop. A good case also does more than protect your phone: it can improve grip, add a stand or wallet, support MagSafe accessories and give your iPhone a completely different look.
There are thousands of iPhone cases to choose from, ranging from inexpensive silicone shells to rugged cases built for serious drop protection. Price isn’t always a reliable guide to quality, either: a cheap case can split, yellow or develop faulty buttons, while spending more doesn’t necessarily mean you’ll get the best case for your needs.
That’s why we hand-test and compare as many iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max cases as we can. We consider protection, materials, build quality, grip, raised screen and camera edges, MagSafe compatibility, weight, useful extras such as stands and card storage, and how the case feels in everyday use. Where manufacturers make specific drop-protection claims, we include those too so you can compare different levels of protection.
In this guide we’ve grouped our recommendations into clear, colorful, protective and leather or faux-leather cases, with options at a range of prices.

Best fun cases for iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max
Best protective cases for iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max

Which type of iPhone case to choose
Apple gives you a handful of finishes; a case gives you thousands—an easy way to make an iPhone 18 Pro look like yours. You can choose a clear case that shows off the iPhone’s original color but adds vital protection, or choose a case with more personality. Protection is key, and some cases will add higher levels of defense than others.
Beyond looks, think about how you use your phone. Want hands-free video? Look for a case with a built-in stand. Want to leave your wallet at home? Choose one with a card storage wallet. And if you charge wirelessly, check for MagSafe compatibility — most cases now offer it, and it’s worth confirming before you buy.





Best clear cases for iPhone 18

Zagg has a whole range of popular scratch-resistant clear case models for the iPhone 18 Pro series, including the Crystal Palace Snap, available with and without a kickstand) and a simpler Lite option without MagSafe and lower but still impressive drop protection. Best protective cases for iPhone 18
As pretty as some iPhone cases are, your principal consideration should be protection. Most decent cases offer reasonable protection, but these protective cases have extra robust features while often adding as little bulk as possible by using the latest, strongest materials. Kevlar is the material used to make bulletproof vests—it’s also known as Aramid Fiber—but I wouldn’t try turning a rifle on it. Graphene is even stronger, and would probably make Superman wince trying to snap it in half.
Other protective iPhone cases don’t worry so much about thinness, and bulk up to protect your iPhone from the worst disasters that can befall it. These might suit you if you work in riskier environments or are an active outdoors iPhone user.
Material matters too: Graphene (elastic yet harder than diamond and up to 200x stronger than steel, according to case makers) or Kevlar (the material used to make bulletproof vests) for serious durability. Kevlar is a type of Aramid Fiber, a strong, heat-resistant synthetic material that gives the material incredible strength and stability.

 FAQ 


1.
What is Apple’s Ceramic Shield protection for iPhones?
Apple introduced Ceramic Shield with the iPhone 12 in 2020, developed jointly with glassmaker Corning, and it’s been standard on every iPhone since (excluding the budget SE line).
It’s made by fusing nano-ceramic crystals into glass, then dipping it in molten salt so potassium ions swap places with smaller sodium ions, creating a compressive surface layer that resists cracking. This gave the original iPhone 12 four times better drop performance than the iPhone 11.
Ceramic Shield 2 arrived with the iPhone 17 lineup in 2025, keeping the same crystal-infusion and ion-exchange process but with a refined composition that’s roughly three times more scratch-resistant than the first generation, while retaining similar drop protection. On the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, Ceramic Shield 2 protects the front, while the back uses Ceramic Shield.





2.
Why do you need an iPhone case?
Your iPhone is a precision device that lives in an unpredictable world—pockets, bags, countertops, pavement. A case is what stands between an accidental drop and a cracked screen or shattered back. It’s not a small risk either: plenty of new iPhone owners crack a screen within the first ten weeks of ownership (source). The IP68 rating means real dust and water resistance, but that’s a lab result—real life is messier. Add in the daily wear of being pulled in and out of a pocket, plus UV exposure over time, and the damage adds up quietly. A case won’t make your iPhone indestructible, but it absorbs the everyday hits so you don’t end up paying for a repair — or a replacement.





3.
Will the iPhone 18 Pro fit a case for the iPhone 17 Pro?
The iPhone 18 Pro series are virtually identical to the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max. Even my iPhone 16 Pro fits in an 18 Pro case, and it works just fine—it looks a bit weird at the back, but otherwise fits nicely. On the other hand, a 17 Pro or 18 Pro wouldn’t fit in a 16 Pro case because of the rear camera positioning. Rokform told Macworld that its iPhone 18 Pro case lineup is compatible with iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro models. However, its older iPhone 17 Pro case lineup is not compatible with iPhone 18 models due to camera plateau design differences. Cases designed with tight tolerances might therefore have a problem as the camera plateau on iPhone 18 Pro/Max is about 0.5mm taller than on iPhone 17 Pro/Max.
Leading case manufacturer OtterBox reports that its iPhone 18 Pro/Max cases are “also compatible with iPhone 17 Pro, so the cases can be used interchangeably between those two models”.
New cases are custom-built for each device to guarantee a perfect fit and protection, so buying a case built specifically for your iPhone model is the safest option. Check our roundup of the Best iPhone 17 Cases and Best iPhone 16 Cases for the older models.





4.
Do I need a screen protector if I use a case?
Yes, it’s still worth using a screen protector even if you have a case, as the two provide different but complementary protection. A case protects the back, corners, and edges of your iPhone, while a screen protector is designed to protect the display itself from scratches and cracks. 
Tempered-glass screen protectors can help absorb direct impacts and protect against everyday scratches and abrasions. A case with a raised screen lip offers some protection if your iPhone lands face down, but it can’t prevent every object or surface from making direct contact with the screen.





5.
What type of iPhone case offers the best protection?
When it comes to maximum protection for your iPhone, the clear winners are rugged cases built with multi-layer materials and military-grade drop ratings. Rugged cases typically combine a hard polycarbonate outer shell with a shock-absorbing TPU (thermoplastic polyurethane) inner layer, reinforced corners, and raised edges around both the screen and camera to prevent direct surface contact on drops.
While silicone and leather cases offer decent everyday scratch protection, they simply can’t match the impact resistance of a purpose-built rugged case.
When choosing a protective case, look for:
Raised screen edge around the front (at least 1mm) to keep the screen safely off surfaces.
Raised camera edge (0.5mm minimum, some go up to 3.6mm).
MIL-STD-810G certification — a U.S. Department of Defense standard for durability.
Reinforced corners for impact absorption.
MagSafe compatibility if you wirelessly charge.





6.
Do I need an iPhone case for iPhone 18?
Many consumers damage their devices each year, with cracked, chipped or shattered screens the leading reason for iPhone repairs. A screen protector is an important first line of defense, but a case with a raised screen edge can much better protect the display from everyday knocks and drops, and tough sides and back will reduce the risk of damage from an accidental fall.
Ceramic Shield 2, introduced with the iPhone 17 generation, protects the front of the iPhone 18 Pro and offers three times better scratch resistance than the iPhone 16 Pro. The back uses Ceramic Shield, which Apple says offers four times better crack resistance than the back glass used on earlier models.
The 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max are the best-protected iPhones yet, but a case is still worth buying. It helps keep that pristine finish looking new and, when it’s time to trade up, a well-protected iPhone can retain far more resale value than the cost of the case itself.





How we test iPhone cases
When we receive new cases, we test them for fit, button feel, grip, MagSafe strength and alignment, raised-edge camera and screen protection, bulk, weight, and day-to-day handling. Where we are unable to test a case ourselves, we assess it based on its specifications and our experience with other cases from the same manufacturer that have impressed us. We report manufacturers’ claimed drop-protection metrics. As we have listed iPhone cases only from trusted companies we feel safe in these claims but note that measurement is the maker’s own and not ours or Apple’s.

title: Apple’s September was huge. October could be even bigger
content:
Macworld





The big September Apple event is over and the new iPhones have been announced, which usually means a little quiet. Not this year. While the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max shipped last month, the star of the show, the iPhone Duo, hasn’t even gone up for pre-order yet.
But that’s not all—there’s a good chance we’re going to see some other new hardware, too. Plus, we’ve got the OS 27.2 updates in testing now with a big update to the Health app, and those will probably be released in October as well. Plus the Matchbox movie premieres! Here’s everything that’s coming in October:
iPhone Duo and other new hardware
We already know Apple has one monster release coming this month, but several other new products could be on the way as well:
iPhone Duo: Pre-orders for Apple’s first folding phone, the iPhone Duo, begin on October 16 and the phone officially becomes available on October 23. Obviously that is going to be the big release of the month, and you can read a lot more about the iPhone Duo in our guide. If you want one, you’ll want to pre-order right when it goes on sale at 8am ET, because we expect stock will be very constrained throughout the rest of this year.
Smart home hub: Leading this month’s rumors is a totally new device we’ve been hearing about for years: a home hub many have taken to calling “HomePad.” It’s a simplified tablet with a roughly 6-inch display that runs a new operating system combining the Standby mode of iPhone, the widgets of Apple Watch, and some of the media capabilities of Apple TV, but without its own app store. It will reportedly control your smart home devices, make FaceTime calls, and recognize faces to automatically adjust to each individual’s preferences. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, the most reliable Apple leaker around, says the device is set to launch on October 13.
HomePod mini 2: Along with the hub, there are persistent rumors of other smart home devices ready to go on sale in October, including a new HomePod mini. The HomePod mini 2 should have a new processor that supports Siri AI, improved networking, and improved audio, but visually resemble the current model, which hasn’t been updated since its 2020 debut. It will likely have a new lineup of colors.
Apple TV 4K (4th gen): The new Apple TV 4K is getting the same treatment: better networking and a faster chip for Siri AI, but otherwise the same as the current models. Some say that the remote might support Find My, with a tiny speaker to make a chime when lost.
iPad mini: Several rumors also claim the next iPad mini is nearly ready for release, with an A20 Pro, OLED display, and landscape-oriented FaceTime camera. It would be a big upgrade, and the most recent rumors say it will launch by the end of October.
M6 MacBook Pro: The M6 has debuted in the Mac mini, and it has been a year since the M5 MacBook Pro, so we now expect a MacBook Pro with M6 to come as early as October. It should be a chip update with the same design.
Touchscreen MacBook Pro: Separate from the regular M6 MacBook Pro, there’s a redesigned MacBook Pro allegedly in the works with an OLED display and a touchscreen. Multiple reports have said it could be ready for release this fall with M5 Pro and M5 Max processors, but chip shortages could also push it into next year.
Apps and software updates
We just got Apple’s biggest yearly software update in ages with last month’s OS 27 launches with the new Siri AI, but there’s a big change coming to it soon.
While the iOS 27.1 release is centered around iPhone Duo and will likely only ship with that device, the OS 27.2 updates — coming for all devices — is already in beta testing and should be widely released in the month of October. The big update for 27.2 is the overhauled Health app, which changes the design to put AI-powered health analysis up front, with collected data on a later tab. With an Apple Watch Series 12 or Ultra 4 and watchOS 27.2, you’ll also get the new Readiness feature.

title: ‘Halo’ and the missed opportunity for the Mac
content:
Macworld





Halo, officially known as Halo: Combat Evolved, was released for the Xbox in 2001. It’s regarded as the game that perfected the first-person shooter on the console, after GoldenEye 007 for the Nintendo 64 had provided the first successful blueprint four years earlier. Yet things could have turned out very differently.
Originally, Halo was unveiled for the Mac at Macworld Expo in July 1999. Alongside other titles, Halo was set to become a flagship for gaming on the Mac. This was no coincidence: the developer, Bungie had made a name for itself on the Mac in previous years with Marathon and Myth. Gaming on the Mac wasn’t exactly a novelty back then. And so Jason Jones, co-founder of Bungie, presented the first gameplay footage of Halo, complete with Martin O’Donnell’s now-iconic theme tune, on a Mac, specifically, the Power Macintosh G3.
Jones was introduced by Steve Jobs himself, who also announced that Halo would be released “early next year,” (early 2000). But things turned out differently.


27 years on, the first gameplay footage from ‘Halo: Combat Evolved’ seems almost prehistoric.



Microsoft buys Bungie
At the same time, Microsoft was planning something quite different. In PC gaming, Apple’s direct competitor had long since established itself and was setting its sights on game consoles. Microsoft wanted to shake up that market, which at the time was dominated by Nintendo, Sony (PlayStation) and, to a lesser extent, Sega (Dreamcast). To succeed, the company had to win gamers over to its platform and offer an attractive game library featuring top-class titles at the console’s launch.
The unveiling of Halo at Macworld Expo came at just the right time. On the one hand, the title promised to breathe new life into the first-person shooter genre; on the other, it was backed by a team that, whilst not as large or well-known as id Software (Doom, Quake), nevertheless already had a solid portfolio to its name. So Microsoft bought Bungie, along with Halo, and the game was not released for the Mac and only for the Xbox in late 2001.
Halo: Combat Evolved did eventually come out for the Mac in 2003, but no further Halo installment has since made it onto an Apple platform natively, even though the series was originally intended for it. You can only play all the titles on Apple devices via the cloud, but to do so you’ll need either Xbox Game Pass Ultimate for Xbox Cloud Gaming or GeForce Now. At least that means you can even play Halo on your iPhone.
The best for (almost) everyone
Halo could have given Mac gaming the boost it needed, but Apple’s gaming dilemma is of its own making. One game wouldn’t have made any difference. It would also be presumptuous to believe that Halo alone could have elevated the platform to a relevant level. After all, many other games–some of which were already better known at the time–were announced back in 1999.
Looking back, Microsoft’s acquisition of Bungie was a great success. Microsoft managed to break into the console market and took Sega’s place, whose Dreamcast flop in 2001 also sealed the company’s fate as a hardware manufacturer.
Halo, on the other hand, established itself as the flagship title for first-person shooters on consoles and brought Bungie immense fame and success within the games industry. Following its split from Microsoft in 2007 and a partnership with Activision since 2010, the studio has, as of 2022, been owned by none other than Sony, Microsoft’s biggest rival in the console market.
And Apple? The company hasn’t completely abandoned its gaming ambitions, but the whole endeavor has been languishing for years. Although Apple makes a decent profit in the sector, it does not operate like a traditional gaming company and almost exclusively as a marketing platform, earning its revenue primarily through commissions from the App Store and in-app purchases. The subscription fees for Apple Arcade won’t feature prominently in the balance sheet.
Still, even without Halo, Apple is posting new record profits year after year. On the whole, things have gone quite well for all three parties involved.

content:
Macworld





At a glance

Our Verdict 
Anyone looking to retrofit an older vehicle with CarPlay and who has sufficient space in the cockpit will find the Lamtto Car Infotainment System to be a solution featuring a large screen, flexible audio output and, as a bonus, a back camera.

When CarPlay was first released, I wasn’t interested, partly because of its limited availability. It was only found in newer cars from more exotic brands. That has changed; many new cars offer CarPlay connectivity, though there are some car companies that aren’t offering it.
Ever since I tried out CarPlay in my second car, I’ve come to view CarPlay more favorably. In fact, I’d hardly want to be without it now. However, my 2008 Renault Kangoo was made before CarPlay became a thing in 2014. The car was retrofitted with a Bluetooth receiver that uses the unused interface of the CD changer (the car really is old!). I’ve been able to listen to music from my iPhone through the car’s impressive sound system.
This is where the Lamtto RC37 Car Infotainment System comes into its own. Unlike other retrofit systems, it connects to the car’s stereo via Aux, FM, or Bluetooth. My car doesn’t have a 3.5-mm jack input, and FM transmitters only work locally at best, where you can still find a free frequency at the edges of the bands and they’re usually useless when on the move, requiring readjustment of the frequency for every transmission area.
More than just a CarPlay screen
The Lamtto comes with three further interesting features: a rear car camera (something my old car wouldn’t even have dared to dream of), a high-resolution 11-inch screen, and pre-installed entertainment apps.
You can stick the 11-inch display onto the dashboard or attach it to the windscreen using a suction cup. I opt for the suction cup, which makes the solution more flexible, as it’s removable, but it does obstruct the field of vision slightly–some may be able to quite literally, look past it. If I tilt the screen significantly lower or mount it on the shelf in front of the radio, I’ll lose sight of it. Sticking the stand on the passenger side is a bad idea because of the airbag. I’ll eventually find the right spot for it.
Setup is absolutely straightforward: switch it on, connect it to the iPhone, launch CarPlay, and you’re done. The Lamtto has a plug that fits into the cigarette lighter socket. This socket also features a USB-A port, which can be used to change and iPhone.
When operating the touchscreen, I found that the suction-cup mounting is less than ideal. The screen always gives way too much when touched. A stand would be the better solution, but then you have to consider a proper mounting area that  is accessible and doesn’t block your windshield. That’s more of a problem with the car and not with the Lamtto kit. At least, thanks to the Bluetooth connection, you can adjust the volume from the steering wheel. And, of course, the connected iPhone responds to Siri.
The system has TikTok, YouTune, and Netflix. They’re off-limits while driving, even if it’s the front passenger using them. Drivers can use them when the car is parked, but this is only of interest to anyone who takes longer driving breaks and whose car battery has sufficient charge.

				
					

				
			
The screen is a nice size, but it can be a bit of a nuisance in your field of vision.

Macwelt




Fiddly setup required for rear camera
The Lamtto’s rear camera is a feature that take it to a whole new level. This isn’t connected wirelessly, but via a cable to the Lamtto display. The manufacturer recommends mounting the camera on or above the license plate–a central position, close to the ground. You’ll need to figure out how to thread the camera’s cable through your car without it getting in the way of your windows or your doors.
The camera switches on automatically when the car is put into reverse. For this to happen you need to attach an additional cable to the positive terminal of the reverse lights of your car. When this lights up, the display receives a signal and shows the camera’s image. That setup is a bit too fiddly for me to do and I’d rather leave it to a professional, who’ll also help me position the display correctly in the car.
Within a very short time of turning on the ignition, the Lamtto device is ready to go, has launched CarPlay, found the iPhone, and resumed the music from where I last left off. Exactly how it should be.
Should you buy the Lamtto RC37? 
The Lamtto Car Entertainment System retrofits older vehicles with CarPlay and also offers a rear camera. The bright 11-inch display can also a disadvantage if you can’t find the right spot to mount it. If you have an 11-inch iPad, you can experiment with it in your car to see if the display would fit and where it wouldn’t get in the way.
Fitting the device in the car and setting it up is completely straightforward once you’ve chosen the right spot. Installing the rear camera requires a steady hand, the sort that car mechanics have.
The pre-installed entertainment apps such as YouTube, Netflix, TikTok and YouTube Music are of interest to those who take longer breaks (such as overnight) in a car park. Even in a traffic jam, and even if the screen is directed only at the front passenger or those in the back seats, watching videos in the car is strongly discouraged.

title: This $100 iPad is the best way to beat the RAM pricing surge
content:
Macworld





		
Aple iPad 8th Generation
View Deal
These days, finding an affordable iPad is darn near impossible. If you want to get one for your kids, then spending a ton of money is definitely not on your to-do list since it’s likely to get dropped or damaged. Well, we’ve found a solution: This Apple iPad 8th Gen is only $110 at Woot but if you use code APPLETEN, it’ll take off another 10 percent, bringing it under $100. It’s not new (Woot says it’s in Grade A Refurbished condition) and won’t get the latest features, but it’s about a third of how much you’d pay for a new iPad today.
The 10.2-inch Retina display is sharp and bright enough for movies, e-books, and homework apps. Inside, the A12 Bionic chip with Neural Engine was a big upgrade for this model. When it came out, it made the 8th-gen iPad much faster than the version before it, and it still handles games, streaming, and everyday apps without much fuss. Back in 2020, we called it “the best affordable tablet you can buy,” and that’s definitely the case right now. The tablet won’t support iOS 27 or Apple Intelligence, but you’re getting a perfect device you don’t have to worry about when you hand it over.
Think about it: Sooner or later, every parent hits the same moment on a long car ride or a rainy Saturday: the kids want your phone, and you’d really like it back. A tablet of their own solves that, but handing a pricey new iPad to a seven-year-old is a gamble most of us would rather skip. Well, at $110, you won’t wince every time your kid “gently” puts it on the table. Because it’s refurbished, you’re also giving a perfectly good device a second life instead of buying new, and a landfill somewhere will thank you. It’s guaranteed to be free of major dents and dings, plus it comes with a 90-day warranty in cases there’s anything wrong with it.
For under $100, this older iPad model is an easy pick if you want a kid-friendly first tablet or a simple spare iPad for the house without paying full price.

title: Leak reveals four colors for Apple’s new smart home hub
content:
Macworld





If the latest reports are correct, we’re less than two weeks away from Apple revealing its long-rumored home hub device. If you’re excited about it and already making plans on how to incorporate it into your home, then you’ll appreciate the latest report that reveals the colors of the new device.
According to a post by itspdfu (who has previously posted leaks that have panned out), Apple will offer four colors for the new device: Rose Pink, Silver, Space Gray, and Starlight. The information was gleaned from a feature itspdfu discovered called Photo Face, which displays four background colors that seemingly match the color of the device.


Apple’s Home device may come in four finishes: Silver, Space Gray, Starlight, and Rose Pink.
The Photo Face setup screen picks its preview art based on the hardware color the device reports.
The device’s housing may also show in setup screens once device assets are available.… https://t.co/8h4iF9OEsG pic.twitter.com/oRRTijUdkO
— pdfu (@itspdfu) October 1, 2026





Notably missing from the color choices is black, but Space Gray could come close enough, depending on the shade Apple uses. Starlight is a light bronze finish that has been offered on the MacBook Air, iPad, and AirPods Max. Apple has offered Rose Gold and Pink devices in the past, but Rose Pink is a new name. However, there were rumors that the iPhone 13 Pro Max was going to come in Rose Pink, but that color never shipped.
The Home hub is expected to have a 6-inch display and come in two forms: a design “reminiscent” of the iMac G4, and another that is mounted to a wall. It’s not clear if Apple will reveal the new smart home products at an event, but rumors point to October 13 as a possible launch date.

title: iPhone 18 Pro Colors Buyer's Guide: Which Should You Choose?
content:
Apple's iPhone 18 Pro and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max models come in four distinct color options, so which should you choose?


The ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ models come in Black, Silver, Glacier, and Burgundy. The aluminum and glass backs are more closely matched than on the iPhone 17 Pro, although the different materials remain somewhat visible.

You should also consider if you plan to use a case with your device and, if so, which one. The ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌'s large, full-width camera plateau stands out on most cases, exposing more of the device's color. Choosing a complimentary color should be your first priority. 

Burgundy

Burgundy is the most distinct and expressive ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ finish, and it is much darker than the ‌iPhone 17‌ Pro's equivalent Cosmic Orange. It looks closer to wine or plum than a vivid red.


Burgundy is the standout shade in the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ lineup, designed to be bold and attention-grabbing. It is the most noticeable ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ color, and the most likely to indicate that you have the latest generation device—there has never been an iPhone color option like it before. 

Burgundy Silicone and TechWoven cases if you want the phone and case to look closely coordinated. With a contrasting case, the large, exposed plateau becomes a prominent patch of red-purple. That is worth considering if you like to change between bright case colors: Burgundy will remain part of every combination.

MagSafe ring covers part of the back. Burgundy is the clearest way to distinguish this generation by color, but anyone hoping for a bright red iPhone may be disappointed. 

Choose Burgundy if you want a distinctive, dark color that remains noticeable even when the phone is in a case.

Glacier

Glacier is a cool, pale blue that gives the iPhone a much softer look than Burgundy. It is much lighter than the ‌iPhone 17‌ Pro's Deep Blue, yet it does not disappear into Silver; in-person, it still looks distinctly blue. 


Glacier is a useful middle ground if you want gentle color with some saturation, without making it the strongest feature of the phone. The exposed camera plateau gives an opaque case a light blue accent, while a clear case reveals most of the finish. Apple's clear case has a large white ‌MagSafe‌ ring, however, so it does not leave the back completely unobstructed.

Apple sells blue cases in shades such as Crisp Blue and Chambray Blue, but neither is named Glacier. If you want the case and phone to match precisely, it may be best to compare them in person; otherwise, a clear or neutral case lets Glacier stand on its own.

Choose Glacier if you want an iPhone with a fresh, subtle, and light appearance.

Silver

Silver is the most classic, versatile, and timeless option, but also the most practical. The finish gives off a clean and bright look that pairs well with virtually any case or wallpaper, and it reflects light more than the other three colors, making it quite neutral.


Its aluminum has a metallic sheen that leans toward white in some lighting conditions. This year, the two rear materials are the same tone, making the new model look much more cohesive than the two-tone Silver ‌iPhone 17‌ Pro.

Silver is also the most adaptable color for cases. The exposed silver plateau provides a crisp, light accent against a dark case and sits more quietly beside a pale one. The color is likely to age well since it goes well with any case and embodies Apple's most traditional colors.

It is also the only finish of the three that pairs well with Apple's own clear case. The clear case's white ‌MagSafe‌ ring is less of a visual interruption here than it is against Black or Burgundy. If you frequently change cases, Silver is unlikely to compete with your next choice.

Unlike Burgundy or Black, Silver minimizes the appearance of damage. When the anodized layer chips or scratches, the raw aluminum underneath is very close in tone, so imperfections blend in far better. For users who prioritize long-term durability of appearance, Silver is the most forgiving finish. It may not be as dramatic as Burgundy or as sleek as Black, but it is the safest choice for maintaining a "like-new" look over years of use.

Choose Silver if you want a classic, flexible look that mitigates the signs of damage.

Black

Black returns after the ‌iPhone 17‌ Pro offered Deep Blue as its darkest option. It offers a dark, neutral look without Deep Blue's blue cast.



A black case makes the exposed camera plateau blend into the rest of the phone. A light or colorful case has the opposite effect, framing a broad dark section across the top. Apple's clear case also makes its white ‌MagSafe‌ ring particularly noticeable against Black, so it is less suited to an uninterrupted all-black look.

If a deep chip or scratch exposes bare aluminum, its lighter color would stand out against this finish, especially on the plateau that Apple's cases leave uncovered. Anyone using the device without a case should be prepared for more noticeable damage. If visible marks would bother you and you plan to go without a case, Silver may be a better fit.

Choose Black if you want a dark, stealthy, and professional look, but be willing to accept signs of wear and tear.
